principle: A business rule decides which rows count and how a result must be qualified. Every rule states its rationale so it can be challenged.

rules.name: Persistency eligible population
rules.statement: Renewal and persistency metrics are computed only over policies with status 'Premium paying (regular)' or 'Lapsed'.
rules.rationale: Persistency_Details contains no row for surrendered or death policies. Using the full policy count as a denominator would understate every renewal rate by including 458 policies that could never have a renewal row.

rules.name: Minimum sample for entity ranking
rules.statement: An entity is ranked on a rate only when its population meets the minimum sample size. Excluded entities are counted and reported, never hidden.
rules.rationale: The median agent has 8 policies and the median branch 3. Without a threshold an agent with 2 policies and 1 lapse would top a lapse ranking at 50%.

rules.name: Unsettled claims excluded from settlement metrics
rules.statement: Settlement-lag and payout metrics cover settled claims only. The claim carrying the 'WIP' sentinel is excluded and the exclusion is reported.
rules.rationale: 'WIP' appears in Status.of.Claim, Amount.Paid and Settlement.Date at once. Treating it as a zero payment would understate the payout ratio; treating it as a settled claim would corrupt the lag distribution.

rules.name: Null supplied metrics excluded, never zeroed
rules.statement: An entity whose supplied metric is null is excluded from rankings on that metric rather than treated as zero, and the excluded count is reported.
rules.rationale: 369 of 1,956 agents have no First Year Persistency Rate. Reading null as zero would place every one of them at the bottom of a persistency ranking on the strength of missing data.

rules.name: Negative durations reported and excluded
rules.statement: A computed duration below zero is excluded from duration statistics and the excluded count is reported. It is never clipped to zero.
rules.rationale: One policy has Login.Date after Inforce.Date. Clipping would silently invent a same-day turnaround; dropping it without saying so would hide a data defect.

rules.name: Personal data withheld from analytical output
rules.statement: Owner.Given.Name and Owner.Comm.Postal.Code are removed from any result returned to a user, in aggregate and record output alike.
rules.rationale: Neither field is needed to answer a portfolio question. Postal code may be read for a data-quality check but is never returned.

rules.name: Outlier fence uses the interquartile range
rules.statement: Outliers are flagged using an interquartile fence at Q1 - k*IQR and Q3 + k*IQR with k = 1.5, not standard deviations.
rules.rationale: The supplied agent rates are heavily skewed and mostly zero, so a mean and standard deviation would be dragged by the very values being tested. A flag is a prompt to look, never a finding.

rules.name: Small-cell rate suppression
rules.statement: A rate computed from fewer than the minimum cell count is suppressed; the count is still shown so the reader sees the population without a misleading rate.
rules.rationale: 134 claims spread across 10 products, 34 states and many age bands leaves cells of one or two. A rate from such a cell is noise presented as a measurement.

rules.name: Policy status definitions
rules.statement: Lapse, in-force, surrender and death are read from POLICY.STATUS and from nothing else. No status is inferred from another field.
rules.rationale: POLICY.STATUS has exactly four values and no status-change date exists. Any attempt to infer a lapse from renewal data would invent a transition the data does not record.

rules.name: Early claim window
rules.statement: An early claim is a death occurring within the configured window of the policy going in force. The window is stated with every result that uses it.
rules.rationale: There is no contestability flag in the data, so 'early' is an analytical convention rather than a contractual status. The default is 365 days.

rules.name: Rounding and presentation
rules.statement: Calculations are carried at full precision and rounded once, at presentation: money to 2 decimals, rates and percentages to 2, ratios to 4, counts as integers.
rules.rationale: Rounding intermediate values compounds error across a multi-step analysis and can make a table's parts disagree with its total.

rules.name: Composite score weights are declared
rules.statement: A composite score is computed from percentile-normalised components using the weights declared here, and the weights are returned with the score.
rules.rationale: The seven supplied agent rates sit on different and undocumented scales, with maxima from 1.28 to 25.96, so they cannot be combined raw. The weighting is an analytical convention, not a company standard, and must be challengeable.

parameters.normalisation: percentile rank within the eligible population
parameters.orientation: every component is oriented so that higher is better

rules.name: Denominator must be declared
rules.statement: Every rate reports the population it was computed over. Figures from different populations are never combined without stating that they differ.
rules.rationale: Policy metrics run over 25,000 rows, renewal metrics over 24,542 and owner metrics over 24,999. Mixing them silently produces a number that is wrong in a way no reader can detect.

rules.name: No causal claim without evidence
rules.statement: An observed difference between groups is reported as an association. A causal claim is made only where the data establishes a mechanism, which these five datasets never do.
rules.rationale: There is no lapse reason, surrender reason, payment history, contact log, underwriting record or intervention history. Every diagnostic is therefore a comparison of observable attributes.

rules.name: Corrupted AppID is not silently repaired
rules.statement: The AppID stored as '1.50E+10' is left as found by default and surfaces as an orphan. A repair is opt-in and is recorded with its justification.
rules.rationale: The mapping to policy 15011000000 is strongly evidenced but still an inference. Applying it silently would put an inference into the data itself.
